title: Repair, Sync & Maintenance
lead: Keeping a long-lived palace consistent, deduplicated, and recoverable.
summary: Seven modules provide incremental-only Palace maintenance: repair.py detects and fixes HNSW index divergence and SQLite corruption with extraction-cap guards; sync.py removes gitignored files using the same matchers as mining; migrate.py rebuilds Palaces across ChromaDB versions; exporter.py streams markdown exports with symlink safety; dedup.py finds near-identical drawers via cosine distance; spellcheck.py auto-corrects user messages while preserving technical terms; sweeper.py catches message-granular content that file-level miners dropped. All critical operations are crash-safe and follow the never-destroy promise.

concepts.definition: Maintenance operations append new data or delete explicitly-marked corrupt entries, but never overwrite existing correct data — a Palace crash mid-operation leaves intact rows untouched.
Safety check in repair.py::check_extraction_safety that aborts rebuild when extracted drawer count (via ChromaDB API) falls short of SQLite ground-truth count, preventing silent data loss.
Stale max_elements setting in HNSW metadata causing it to report fewer capacity than SQLite rows, eventually triggering segfaults — detected via hnsw_capacity_status and fixed by rebuild.
SQLite max_seq_id row corrupted by shim misfire, holding ~1.23e18 integer that silently suppresses queue writes; repaired via heuristic (collection MAX) or sidecar restoration.
Deterministic drawer IDs (e.g. sweep_SESSION_UUID) that allow re-upsert to idempotently dedupe on reruns, making sweeper and other ingest paths resumable after failure.
sync.py uses the same GitignoreMatcher infrastructure as miner.py, so files excluded from mining are also removed from Palace during sync if they become gitignored.
SQLite full-text-search index that can become inconsistent after multiple collection deletes; repair.py::_vacuum_and_rebuild_fts5 atomically reconstructs it without touching row data.
exporter.py::_safe_open_for_write uses O_NOFOLLOW on POSIX and pre-checks os.path.islink on Windows to prevent pre-placed symlinks from redirecting writes to system directories.

symbols.name: check_extraction_safety
symbols.role: Guards against silent data loss when extracted count diverges from SQLite ground-truth; raises TruncationDetected with recovery instructions.

symbols.name: rebuild_from_sqlite
symbols.role: Bypass-API recovery path for #1308 HNSW corruption; extracts via raw SQLite reads, re-embeds, and upserts into fresh Palace with atomic swap.

symbols.name: sync_palace
symbols.role: Main entry: removes gitignored/missing/out-of-scope drawers using same GitignoreMatcher infrastructure as mining.

symbols.name: TruncationDetected
symbols.role: Raised by extraction-cap guard when recovery is needed; carries human-readable message and counts for operator decision.

symbols.name: extract_via_sqlite
symbols.role: Yields (embedding_id, document, metadata) directly from SQLite, used by rebuild_from_sqlite when ChromaDB API fails.

symbols.name: migrate
symbols.role: Rebuilds Palace when ChromaDB version diverges; detects version, extracts, validates write round-trip, then atomically swaps.

symbols.name: export_palace
symbols.role: Streams drawers in paginated batches to markdown files, with O_NOFOLLOW symlink defense.

symbols.name: dedup_palace
symbols.role: Main entry: groups drawers by source_file, applies greedy dedup within threshold, reports deletions.

symbols.name: spellcheck_user_text
symbols.role: Corrects user messages token-by-token, preserving technical terms, URLs, known names, and capitalized words.

symbols.name: sweep
symbols.role: Ingest every message in .jsonl file not already represented, using deterministic IDs and per-session cursors for idempotent reruns.

symbols.name: RebuildCollectionError
symbols.role: Raised when temp rebuild fails; carries live_replaced flag so caller knows whether to restore or leave Palace intact.

symbols.name: _safe_open_for_write
symbols.role: Opens file for writing with O_NOFOLLOW (POSIX) and pre-check (Windows) to block symlink-based write redirection.

surprises.title: Metadata sanitization coercion on empty dict
surprises.detail: Lines 150-154 in repair.py: when extracted drawers have None or {} metadata (from sparse historical writes), repair coerces to {"_repaired_empty_meta": True} to pass chromadb 1.5.x upsert validation. The sentinel is discoverable later via where={"_repaired_empty_meta": True}, turning a silent failure into a queryable state.

surprises.title: Poisoned max_seq_id detection uses float64 ceiling (2^53)
surprises.detail: Lines 1336-1342 in repair.py: the threshold for detecting corrupted max_seq_id rows is 1 << 53 (~9e15), chosen because real embeddings_queue seq_ids never reach that magnitude and the 0.6.x shim's misfire yields ~1.23e18, safely above the threshold. A clever heuristic that avoids false positives.

surprises.title: Cursor comparison uses lexical < on ISO-8601 strings
surprises.detail: Lines 147-177 in sweeper.py: get_palace_cursor returns max(timestamps) and the sweep compares via < cursor without parsing. ISO-8601 strings sort lexically in the correct order, so no date parsing is needed. This is both elegant and avoids timezone misinterpretation.

surprises.title: Greedy dedup sorts by document length, keeps longest
surprises.detail: Lines 79-128 in dedup.py: the dedup_source_group function sorts by doc length descending and keeps if not too similar to already-kept drawers. Not optimal for lossy dedup (shortest are often noise), but deterministic and recoverable.

surprises.title: Sync's strict apply safety: requires explicit scope
surprises.detail: Lines 224-229 in sync.py: apply mode (dry_run=False) refuses to run without explicit wing= or project_dirs=, preventing accidental full-palace pruning. Auto-detection is only enabled in dry-run mode, a safety-by-design pattern.

surprises.title: Spellcheck edit-distance guard varies by word length
surprises.detail: Lines 202-208 in spellcheck.py: max_edits is 2 for words ≤7 chars, 3 for longer. This prevents autocorrect from turning 'a' into 'the' while allowing 'knoe' → 'know'. A pragmatic guard against over-aggressive correction.

designDecisions.decision: Backup only SQLite, not HNSW files, during repair rebuild
designDecisions.rationale: HNSW binary files can grow to terabytes on corrupted Palaces; backing up only chroma.sqlite3 (source of truth) makes recovery instant while preserving the ability to restore. Aligns with 'incremental only' — the rebuild path never needs the old HNSW files, only the SQLite rows.

designDecisions.decision: Extraction-cap guard aborts rather than auto-overrides
designDecisions.rationale: Issue #1208 showed a Palace with 67,580 drawers on disk but only 10,000 returned via ChromaDB API. Silently destroying 57,580 rows is unacceptable. The guard forces explicit user acknowledgement (--confirm-truncation-ok) after independent verification, honoring the 'never destroy' promise.

designDecisions.decision: Sync holds mine_palace_lock for entire classify+apply, not per-batch
designDecisions.rationale: Ensures snapshot consistency between the classification pass and the deletion pass, preventing race conditions where a file is classified 'gitignored' then re-mined before deletion.
Capitalized words are likely proper nouns or intentional emphasis; touching them risks correcting names (Riley → riley) or domain terms (HTML → html). The only safe move is to leave them alone.

designDecisions.decision: Sweeper uses message-granular dedup, not file-level
designDecisions.rationale: File-level miners (miner.py, convo_miner.py) chunk at fixed byte sizes and don't track message boundaries. The sweeper catches message-level content and dedupes via deterministic ID, allowing re-run safety without re-chunking transcripts.

stats.label: Safety guards
stats.value: 6+ (extraction-cap, poisoned max_seq_id, HNSW divergence, symlink defense, live_replaced tracking, write round-trip validation)

related.why: Maintenance operations depend on ChromaBackend for collection lifecycle and direct SQLite access for recovery paths.
Maintenance concepts like drawers, wings, rooms, and closets are defined by the Palace model; repair/sync/export all operate on these structures.
Exporter's symlink defense and spellcheck's entity-registry preservation align with security-by-architecture and privacy-preserving design.
Sweeper complements file-level miners by catching message-granular content; sync uses the same gitignore matcher infrastructure as miner.py.
Spellcheck integrates optional autocorrect and entity registry; repair's extraction-cap guard is informed by understanding of ChromaDB's internal limits.

searchDoc.title: Repair, Sync & Maintenance
searchDoc.summary: Seven modules provide incremental-only Palace maintenance: repair, sync, migrate, export, dedup, spellcheck, and sweep. All operations are crash-safe and follow the never-destroy promise.
searchDoc.body: The MemPalace maintenance area is seven modules that keep a long-lived Palace consistent, deduplicated, and recoverable. Every operation obeys an incremental-only invariant: it appends new data or deletes explicitly-marked corrupt entries, but never overwrites existing correct rows, so a crash mid-operation leaves intact data untouched. repair.py offers four tiers: status (read-only health check comparing SQLite row count vs HNSW element count), scan (find unfetchable drawer IDs), prune (delete only corrupt IDs), and rebuild (extract all, back up only chroma.sqlite3, delete and recreate the collection, re-upsert). The extraction-cap guard from issue 1208 checks SQLite directly before any destructive operation; if SQLite reports more drawers than extraction yielded, rebuild aborts with recovery instructions rather than silently destroying data. The real case had 67,580 drawers on disk but only 10,000 returned through the ChromaDB API. Poisoned max_seq_id rows from a 0.6.x shim misfire are detected using a 2 to the 53rd power threshold, the float64 exact-integer ceiling, and un-poisoned non-destructively. Rebuilds use a two-phase live swap staging into a temp collection first and tracking a live_replaced flag for recovery. The FTS5 full-text index is atomically rebuilt and SQLite pages reclaimed via VACUUM. sync.py removes drawers whose source files are now gitignored, deleted, or out of scope, reusing the same GitignoreMatcher infrastructure as miner.py, holding the mine lock for the whole classify and apply window. Apply mode refuses to run without explicit wing or project_dirs scope. migrate.py rebuilds a Palace across ChromaDB versions, extracting directly from chroma.sqlite3 when the API fails, validating a write round-trip to catch silent-drop failures, then atomically swapping with an EXDEV copy-and-delete fallback and rollback guards. exporter.py streams drawers in paginated batches of 1000 to markdown organized by wing and room, with O_NOFOLLOW symlink defense closing the TOCTOU window. dedup.py groups drawers by source_file and consolidates near-identical drawers by cosine distance, greedily keeping the longest version. spellcheck.py corrects user messages while preserving technical terms, URLs, CamelCase, ALL_CAPS, words with digits, and known entity names. sweeper.py ingests Claude Code jsonl transcripts message-by-message using deterministic IDs like sweep_SESSION_UUID and per-session ISO-8601 cursors for idempotent, resume-safe reruns.
